agent_data_note: Use mounted SV-COMP 2024 (+ optional 2023) under `dataset_candidate/hetrify-svcomp/`. Construct RISC-V assembly / missing-function / binary tasks as in Hetrify (ICSE 2025). Backend verifier is CBMC; compile with riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc. Prefer real SV-COMP tasks over invented C. Report reduced timeouts/unwind when sandbox RAM << 384GB.
benchmark_rules: Pool: SV-COMP C verification tasks; paper used 100 small (1–3 funcs) + 30 large (>5 funcs, >300 LOC) constructable subsets.
Compile unverifiable segments / programs with riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc to assembly, static libs, or binaries as needed.
Convert RISC-V assembly/binary (or missing closed-source segments) to verifiable C with semantic-equivalence guarantees (Hetrify-style), then verify with CBMC.
Baselines: direct CBMC on stubs for missing functions; Ghidra decompile→CBMC when available; IDA Pro is commercial and usually unavailable — document skip.
Primary metrics: Correctness Rate = Correct / Total; Error Rate = 1 - (Correct + Timeouts) / Total.
Paper protocol: timeout 3000s; correct programs unwind=20; incorrect: no fixed unwind. If resource-limited, use a disclosed reduced protocol on a smaller subset.
Shared mount is read-only. Copy selected tasks under `project/` before modification; write results under `project/` or `results/`.
non_goals: Claiming full 384GB dual-EPYC reproduction without matching hardware
Using IDA Pro without a licensed install
Fabricating SV-COMP-like tasks unrelated to the mounted benchmarks
Skipping CBMC entirely in favor of informal testing only
